title: Warmth gave no clear common link to stop-order frog richness contrasts in four US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether survey-night warmth changed recorded frog richness between stops 8-10 and stops 1-3 on NAAMP routes. Four tests used 7,375 runs in the Northeast and Midwest in 2001-2008 and 2009-2015. Models controlled route, observer, survey window, year, season, wind and rain reports. All four estimated slopes were positive, from 0.030 to 0.071 recorded groups per stop per 5 C. Three four-test intervals included zero. The later Midwest interval was positive, but it included zero with the largest of three cluster error estimates and in the subset with traffic and noise reports. Site-sequence, cooling and duration checks kept positive point slopes. These data did not establish a common link across all four samples. Stop number is only a timing proxy. Selected nights, changing habitat, few year clusters and mixed calling and hearing effects limit inference. This is not a test of true richness, a climate trend or pollution. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Warmth slopes for stop-order richness contrasts. Main intervals use route and year clusters. The max_se check uses the largest route, year or two-way standard error. Noise intervals use the selected subset with traffic and noise reports. Intervals account for four main tests.
